root_cause.text: `skb_kfree_head()` in `net/core/skbuff.c` tried to infer whether an skb head came from `skb_small_head_cache` by comparing `end_offset`, but under KFENCE `ksize()` returns the exact requested size, causing a kmalloc-allocated skb head to be misclassified and freed to the wrong slab cache.
root_cause.evidence: The patch removes the `if (end_offset == SKB_SMALL_HEAD_HEADROOM) kmem_cache_free(net_hotdata.skb_small_head_cache, head); else kfree(head);` logic and replaces it with unconditional `kfree(head)`, while the CVE explains that KFENCE makes `slab_build_skb() -> ksize()` return the requested size, which makes `skb_end_offset` match `SKB_SMALL_HEAD_HEADROOM` and triggers the cross-cache free (`kmem_cache_free(skbuff_small_head): Wrong slab cache. Expected skbuff_small_head but got kmalloc-1k`).

agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch removes the `if (end_offset == SKB_SMALL_HEAD_HEADROOM) kmem_cache_free(net_hotdata.skb_small_head_cache, head); else kfree(head);` logic and replaces it with unconditional `kfree(head)`, while the CVE explains that KFENCE makes `slab_build_skb() -> ksize()` return the requested size, which makes `skb_end_offset` match `SKB_SMALL_HEAD_HEADROOM` and triggers the cross-cache free (`kmem_cache_free(skbuff_small_head): Wrong slab cache. Expected skbuff_small_head but got kmalloc-1k`).

intent_record.intent_summary: Simplify skb head freeing to always use kfree(), removing the special-case slab free path.
intent_record.what: The conditional in skb_kfree_head() was removed, and the function now always calls kfree(head) instead of choosing between kmem_cache_free(net_hotdata.skb_small_head_cache, head) and kfree(head) based on end_offset.
intent_record.how: At runtime, skb head memory is no longer freed through the skb_small_head_cache slab path even when end_offset equals SKB_SMALL_HEAD_HEADROOM; all callers now release the head with the generic kfree() path, changing the deallocation behavior for small heads.

grouping_result.intent: Simplify skb head freeing to always use kfree(), removing the special-case slab free path.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly targets skb head freeing in skb_kfree_head(), removing the faulty cache-specific slab free logic that misclassified kmalloc heads under KFENCE. This addresses the root cause.

candidates.rationale: This conditional is the flawed size-based heuristic used to decide whether the skb head should be freed from skb_small_head_cache. Under KFENCE, ksizes can match the requested size exactly, causing kmalloc-allocated heads to be misclassified and sent to the wrong free path.

This is the incorrect free operation triggered by the misclassification. A kmalloc-allocated skb head can be incorrectly freed to the small-head slab cache, which is the direct consequence of the buggy inference.

vuln_statements.explanation: This size-based check is the faulty heuristic that tries to infer whether the skb head belongs to skb_small_head_cache. Under KFENCE, ksize() can equal the requested size, so a kmalloc-allocated head may satisfy this condition and be misclassified.
This is the incorrect free path reached after the misclassification. A kmalloc-allocated skb head can be freed to the small-head slab cache instead of the proper allocator, causing the vulnerability.

Author: Eric Dumazet <edumazet@google.com>

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct described in the root cause is a misclassification in skb_kfree_head() due to using an end_offset comparison that can match the wrong allocator under KFENCE. This snippet shows the new helper: `static void skb_kfree_head(void *head, unsigned int end_offset)` and the decision `if (end_offset == SKB_SMALL_HEAD_HEADROOM) kmem_cache_free(skb_small_head_cache, head); else kfree(head);`. In this commit, the code does not infer the cache from a generic kmalloc size; it explicitly routes only the dedicated small-head allocation size to `skb_small_head_cache` and otherwise uses `kfree()`. The allocator path also tags those allocations by setting `*size = SKB_SMALL_HEAD_CACHE_SIZE`, and frees call `skb_kfree_head(..., skb_end_offset(skb))` or `skb_kfree_head(data, size)` consistently. So the old bug condition is not present here, and the fix is already present in this function body.
